Heard.

Instant application has been preferred by the applicants namely Ram Prasad S/o Ram Dularey, Ravi Kumar S/o Ram Prasad, Suresh Kumar Raidas S/o Nanhkau and Akash S/o Jai Ram for following relief:
"to quash the entire proceeding of complaint case no. 1146/2015 under Section 323/504/506 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District Unnao as well as impugned summoning order dated 22.2.2016 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ram Prasad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. ... on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63450397/
1 Court no. 5 Unnao Kaushal Kishor.....Vs......Ravi Kumar and others, as contained in Annexure no. 1 to this petition."
It is stated that on account of matrimonial dispute between Anurag Kureel, an Advocate and Meenu Kumari W/o Anurag Kureel D/o Ram Prasad (applicant no. 1), an FIR was lodged i.e. Case Crime No. 0433 on 21.07.2015 by Meenu Kumari making allegations therein to attract offense under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against Anurag Kureel (husband), Ramvati (mother-in-law) and Virag (brother in law) and in retaliation, Kaushal Kishore,
at the behest of his friend Anurag Kureel, filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. which was treated as complaint case registered as Complaint Case no. 1146 of 2015 (Kaushal Kishore Vs.
Ravi Kumar and Others) and in the said case, vide order dated 22.02.2016 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 5 Unnao, the applicants were summoned and during the pendency of the case arising out of Case Crime No. 0433, indicated above, the dispute between Anurag Kureel. and Meenu Kumari was settled and now both the persons are living happily as husband and wife under one roof and in this view of this matter, the parties have entered into a compromise and a copy of compromise deed, duly signed by the parties, is annexed as Annexure No. SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit (IA No. 4 of 2024).

sentences.text: As such, keeping in view the settlement arrived at between the parties and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in this regard, the proceedings impugned are liable to be quashed.

Whether the parties have, in fact, compromised the matter or not, can best be ascertained by the Trial Court as such compromise has to be duly verified in presence of the parties concerned before the Court.

Considering the aforesaid, this application is disposed of finally in following terms:-
(i) The parties to the proceedings in issue shall appear and file the compromise before the concerned Court within four week's from today.
(ii) If the parties appear before the concerned Court in terms of above, the concerned Court shall proceed to verify the compromise between the parties to the proceedings and prepare a report to the same effect and the original compromise deed be made part of record.
(iii) The concerned Court shall conclude the process of verification of compromise within two week's from the date of production of copy of this order.
(iv) The concerned Court shall permit the parties to the proceedings to obtain the certified copy of the report as well as compromise deed.
(v) It shall be open to the applicant(s) to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.
